one_liner: A uniformed U.S. Public Health Service officer job overseeing ICE Health Service Corps medical staffing contracts as Program Manager and Contracting Officer's Representative.
fit_summary: Only current commissioned USPHS officers can apply, so Daniel cannot be considered. It also requires a degree that qualifies for a USPHS category, COR Level I certification and federal healthcare contract management, none of which are on his resume.
eligibility: Only current USPHS commissioned officers may apply; Call to Active Duty (CAD) candidates are excluded, and the 'public' hiring-path label does not override this.
Requires a qualifying degree for the officer's category plus an advanced degree (e.g., MPH, M.A., M.S.) from an accredited institution.
Requires 3-5 years of professional experience in the officer's category, including at least 2 years in program management, administration, and evaluation.
Requires Contracting Officer Representative (COR) Level I certification at entry, with COR Level II/III required within 12 months.
Must maintain PHS basic readiness criteria; this is an O-5 (Commander) billet.
strategy: Do not apply; the status restriction is absolute, and an application from a non-officer will be screened out at the minimum-qualifications check.
Use this posting as a map of contract-oversight skills: search USAJOBS for civilian GS-1101/0343/0340 program analyst or COR-support roles open to the public at DHS, FEMA, or ICE.

Frame your IEM work in these terms if it fits truthfully, such as supporting government client deliverables, performance reporting, and stakeholder coordination on emergency management contracts, viewed from the contractor side.
Consider earning FAC-COR Level I through the free FAI training, which is often open to the public, and look at entry-level acquisition roles (GS-1102) to build toward jobs like this one.
If you ever pursue USPHS commissioning, know that it requires a qualifying health-profession degree; with a policy background, that is likely not a practical route.
interview_questions: Describe how you have monitored contractor performance and handled a deficiency.
How would you review an invoice for accuracy against contract terms and the FAR?
Tell us about a time you resolved a conflict among multiple stakeholders.
How do you align project milestones and risks with organizational priorities?
watch_outs: Status-only: the job is restricted to current USPHS officers, so Daniel is ineligible.
Requires an advanced degree and COR Level I certification at hire.
Location is negotiable after selection, and occasional travel is required.
